newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish committee proposes to allow share buybacks.
newsitem.headline: Swedish committee proposes to allow share buybacks.

text.p: The Swedish company law committee will on Monday propose Swedish corporations will be allowed to buy back their own shares.
"The committee will propose that corporations will be allowed to buy back their own shares and that this rule will be valid as of January 1, 1999," Rolf Skog, secretary to the comittee, told Reuters.
The law cannot be valid earlier because the committee is proposing to change almost half of the total corporation legislation and this process will take time, Skog said.
"There are numerous other changes, but I do not want to reveal any of them until Monday," he said.
Several Swedish companies, among them automotive group AB Volvo, have previously said they would be interested in buying back their own shares if it becomes allowed.
With share buyback not permitted, several companies have in recent months have announced share redemption programmes. These include Volvo, engineer Sandvik, and insurer Trygg-Hansa.
